I mean come on, a lot of people are afraid to die, but here I am literally chasing death. I shouldn't be afraid of anything life related whether it's failure, loneliness, loss, childhood trauma or illnesses and diseases. If I'm ready to die and have accepted the thought of death, I should be ready for anything. Death is always the worst case scenario, so the other things  aren't going to be that serious anyway.

Life has always been bad, unjust, unfair and hard. Doesn't matter whether you had lived in 3rd century or 21st. They always say "it gets better" it doesn't. It's always you that gets better not life. Life is always the same miserable thing, you're the one who grows and gets better at handling it over time. Also, I've realized that I have grown so much as a person because of pain, I've been seeing life for what it is, I have met my worst side, I have faced my demons and most importantly it makes me appreciate the people who despite all the difficulties still want to go on, despite all the evil still are good, despite all the lie still are honest. Maybe if we don't go through this, we don't grow to be that best version of us that we're going to be in the future. It's our response to these difficulties and our wisdom defines us . "Life is not worth the suffering" I say that everyday, but now I'm thinking "make life be worth the suffering".

My story: believe it or not, it does get better; but it also never really goes away When I attempted, 19 years ago now I called the suicide hotline. Next thing I knew, firemen and cops came. I freaked out. I bit the fireman who was holding onto me too tightly. Obviously, it didn't do anything through his gear. They cuffed me to a gurney and loaded me into the ambulance. I was treated like shit at the ER. My (now ex) husband was angry with me. ANGRY! He wasn't worried about my well-being, just how it made him look. It was all horrible. 

Ten years later, I was ready to try again but decided to wait until I got paid, which would be a Wednesday. That Monday, I got scared and got an appointment to see my psychiatrist so I could ask to go to the psych hospital because I was not safe. The doctor left me and my husband in his office to call the hospital and tell them I would be a self-admit, rather than a legal hold, since I came in asking to go. While alone with my husband, he asked if everything I told the doctor was true. This was after weeks if me sobbing nightly and about a week if telling him I didn't want to live. It was like here didn't hear me until the doctor acknowledged it. 

There's a reason he's my ex. And I'm not sorry he has stage 4 lymphoma. Neither is our son, so that's saying something. But that's beside the point.

Anyway, it's been another 9 years, almost exactly (I went to the psych hospital January 31, 2012. The first attempt was February 2, 2002. This is a bad time of year for me). I've been in therapy nearly constantly since and on one med after another. I've been in a much healthier relationship the last 5 years and a job that is fulfilling for me, while allowing me to work with my multiple health issues, for the last 8.5.  Going to the psych hospital helped a lot, but only because I wanted it to. I feel the same about therapy. I still see a therapist monthly (I see her virtually this Thursday), but I'm so much more stable now that it is really just a check-in. That isn't to say I'm completely better. I've just gotten rid of so many toxic parts of my life and have finally started finding myself again.

Still, I do firmly believe that once a person see suicide as an option, it's always an option. When my rabbit died in 2017, I almost followed him. In 2018, I found myself in a terrible spot where what was supposed to be a blessing turned into a nightmare. I almost hiked into the woods, never to return. In 2019, the shit continued to pile on. I had just moved back to Vegas with my SO and we had nowhere to go. I couldn't take all the pressure and almost lost myself then (you can see what happened in one of my first Reddit posts to this very sub). I was helped by a kind stranger. Even the little things can trigger that voice. Failed a test? My life is over now! Stubbed my toe? Oh, guess I gotta kill myself! Over time, that voice gets easier to ignore. I promise.
 
I'm still struggling significantly financially. But I've come to realize the rest is so much better, I can deal with the poverty. I have friends now, which ex-husband didn't allow. My family is good to me. My SO and I recently invited a close friend into our relationship. I'm loved. I'm not cured, but it does get better.

I'm bad at keeping promises When I was 14 or so I promised myself that I'd kill myself after my 18th birthday, but then, so many good things happened. I went from a lonely person to someone with friends who made my life feel worth it, I went from someone who just spent their evenings alone to someone who got invited to things. I went from a person who doubted it was even possible that I'd ever be loved, to someone who experienced what I still think is true love. For some people the story ended at that high point, for some people they just go through their life with good friends and a SO who loves them no matter what, and that person then lives a happy and long life.That person isn't me. 

Last year within my group of good friends, the people who I would have died for, a breakup happened, and I, the fool I am, fell in love with the girl who got broken up with. Some may have brought up the so called "bro code" one did in fact, that person brought it up after they found out about me and her, he hosted all the get togethers, and from when he found out, well, let's just say the getting invited to things stopped. 

There were still people around, but they all drifted away. At the time all I saw it as was the end of a chapter of my life, the ending of that but what I got in return was the love of my life, I thought that I could handle having fewer friends, as long as I had her, that I didn't need all these people as my reasons to live. That I didn't need a big group of friends if I had the best friend I could possibly have.

I think you can see where this is going. 

She left me, the person who I loved more than anything else, someone once said it is better to have loved and lost than never loved at all, that person, was dumb. The pain it brings to lose someone, it's greater than anything I could have imagined before now. All that's keeping me going is just a desperate hope that she'll change her mind, that she'll realise she still loves me and wants me, that's the last pathetic hope I'm clinging to, and it's not one I think is likely. Because the world isn't built on what we want to happen.

All I can think about is how when she gets with someone else, it'll be the last thing I need convince myself to just kill myself, the straw that broke the camel's back so to speak. I can't help but wish it would just happen sooner rather than later, at least then I'll have to let go of that little hope I can't seem to shake, then I can truly and finally give up on living. 

But instead of that I've come to a decision, this year is it, either my life turns around by the end of this year, either things get better is some truly meaningful way. Or I'll know, there's no point in hope for the future, I'll know that it's time, that I've seen all the good things from life I ever will see. And when I reach that deadline (perhaps a literal one) if it's not better by then, I'll end my life.

TL;DR I'm not entirely ready to give up on my last hope for the future, so I'm giving it until the end of the year before I decide if I want to continue living.

Really Struggling Because Of COVID Hi, I'm 19 years old (bordering on 20) and I've been struggling really hard recently. I'm trans and living with my family; I haven't come out to them, they very obviously wouldn't be supportive and I believe that it would at best introduce more tension into our relationship and at worst leave me homeless or potentially physically hurt. I feel like business acquittances with my near family and every conversation I have with them gives me an intense feeling of anxiety because they can be very cruel verbally seemingly out of nowhere. (It feels as I can't really express myself in a genuine way, I have to speak in a way that keeps them from being emotionally abusive to me.)

I've largely accepted this as a "their fault" sort of thing and a few years ago I decided to move away and in with some friends. COVID has thrown a very serious wrench into that plan; I was a very big shut-in type up until like, halfway through 2019. I strongly suspect that I have OCD (though I'm hesitant to say for sure without a diagnosis, seeking real psychological care feels out of the question now financially) because I've had this horrible anxiety of there being a "dirt" or "infection" that other people had that would "pass on" to me when they touched me. I've had lots of social interactions go south and generally had a really awful time being outside and talking to people person-to-person because of this, but I was starting to adjust and see the outside world in a more positive light before COVID really started to hit here.

It feels like a horrible cruel irony that my unfounded anxiety that kept me homebound has become a genuine real thing. I feel like if this had happened to me even a year ago I would've felt great about it, like it would've felt like I would be able to relate the way I felt to other people by comparing it to COVID. Now I just feel awful, because all I really want to do now is go around and be around people, but my anxiety has been rekindled by the very Real threat of getting a disease and I haven't gone very far from my house since the start of it.

I've interacted with my friends online through discord calls and generally kept in touch, but I feel like I both totally depend on this and use the app in a very unhealthy way. When I speak to them, I'm almost keeping score of how well I'm doing; when I tell a joke for instance, I'll have this feeling of "will they laugh?" where I get very anxious. If they do laugh, I don't exactly feel Good, I just feel a relief of tension. If they don't, it sticks with me for the night or until the next time I get to talk with them and just repeats itself in my head. 

The only people I see in person are very toxic to me, so I depend on my friends to have like, any social interaction, which is a need I very desperately have to fill. On our personal discord server, we have open voice channels where you can join without notifying the others. The idea is that if you want to talk to people but don't specifically want to bother them (you can probably read more deeply into Why Someone Would Want To Do This I Think) you can enter the channel, and if someone sees you and wants to chat, they can pop in. I obsess over this. I check it almost constantly, and whenever I see them sitting there, waiting to talk, I get performance anxiety. I almost feel like this is the only thing that makes me feel like a person anymore- everything else is just filler. Even the way I think, my "inner voice", has been reframed; I *think* like I'm talking to them. When I see something, my inner monologue plays out *how I would describe what happened to me to my friends directly*, like my whole life is dominated by presenting what happens to me to others.

I don't even feel like I have a meaningful relationship now that I don't ever see anybody in person. I feel a lot more like I'm entertaining them instead of relating to them like I used to. Whenever I'm not cracking jokes or being witty it feels like there's this Dead Air or Awkward Silence, and it makes me feel like I'm actively failing to talk to them. I keep trying to inquire about how they feel, to get them to tell me about what's on their mind or how their day was or what they think about something I'm speaking on, but their answers feel so minimal and shallow, as if they're trying to avoid speaking to me. At times I feel like a shitty podcast with light interactive elements; they don't even listen to me consistently. Oftentimes they'll tune me out or mute me without telling me so they can watch a video or something. It's horribly degrading and it's made me feel like less of a person. But I depend on these calls to feel *anything*. When I'm alone they're all I can really think about; that or awful self deprecating suicidal thoughts.
